NO

The script drops block 15 instead of block 14: its `DROP` set is `{2, 6, 10, 15}`, while Required result clause 1 says to remove blocks 2, 6, 10, 14. As a consequence, old block 14 survives and is renumbered to 11, whereas clause 2 requires old 15 to become 11 and old 14 to be deleted. The script's own checks (12 contiguous layers, 86 tensors) still pass, so the error is silent, but the values in output block 11 come from the wrong source block and will fail the bit-exact comparison in Grading.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
